podcast.body: This "12-week number one smash" served as many Americans' introduction to the sound of Crunk, a Southern Rap subgenre pioneered by Lil Jon. Despite its immense cultural relevance and commercial success, winning three R&B genre Grammys, it controversially lost Record of the Year to Ray Charles and Nora Jones's "Here We Go Again" in 2005. "Usher's 12-week number one smash in 2004, and the lead single to his diamond-selling blockbuster album Confessions, was many Americans' introduction to the sound of Crunk, the Southern Rap Subgenre pioneered by Lil Jon."

podcast.body: This song featuring Lil Jon and Ludacris was the Billboard year-end number one for 2004, spending 12 weeks at number one. It is considered the "ultimate bottle service jam," combining Usher's R&B Lothario persona with Lil Jon's Atlanta Crunk Sound at its peak, plus a "killer Ludacris route." Usher's dominance in 2004 included four number one singles and a Diamond-certified album, "Confessions." "Usher owned 2004 with four number one singles and an album, Confessions That Went Diamond."
